basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/Silverfort/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The [Silverfort](https://silverfort.com) ITDR Admin Console connector solution allows ingestion of Silverfort events and logging into Microsoft Sentinel. Silverfort provides syslog based events and logging using Common Event Format (CEF). By forwarding your Silverfort ITDR Admin Console CEF data into Microsoft Sentinel, you can take advantage of Sentinels's search & correlation, alerting, and threat intelligence enrichment on Silverfort data. Please contact Silverfort or consult the Silverfort documentation for more information. **Data Connectors:** 1, **Workbooks:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 20 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This solution installs workbook(s) to help you gain insights into the telemetry collected in Microsoft Sentinel. After installing the solution, start using the workbook in Manage solution view.

The [Silverfort](https://silverfort.com) ITDR Admin Console connector solution allows ingestion of Silverfort events and logging into Microsoft Sentinel.
 Silverfort provides syslog based events and logging using Common Event Format (CEF). By forwarding your Silverfort ITDR Admin Console CEF data into Microsoft Sentinel, you can take advantage of Sentinels's search & correlation, alerting, and threat intelligence enrichment on Silverfort data. 
 Please contact Silverfort or consult the Silverfort documentation for more information.
This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.
An Active Directory domain privilege escalation vulnerability that enables a privileged user to access the Domain Controller by abusing Active Directory Certificate Service
Vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems by exploiting a flaw in the way Log4j handles log messages containing specially crafted strings
The NoPac vulnerability involves privilege escalation, allowing attackers to gain unauthorized access and potentially take control of an entire Active Directory domain
A security weakness that allows attackers to gain unauthorized access to user accounts by systematically guessing the username and password combinations.

Detects Silverfort Lateral Movement Advance Path incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects sequential authentications between different systems. May indicate attacker progression through the network post-compromise.

Detects Silverfort Credential Scanning incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects multiple failed login attempts to the same server from several different accounts within a short time period. May indicate credential scanning or early-stage brute-force activity.

Detects Silverfort Lateral Movement Search Path incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects bursts of authentications from one host to many others. May indicate reconnaissance for lateral movement targets.

Detects Silverfort User Denied Suspicious Authentications incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects denied MFA with other risk indicators (e.g., new host, impossible travel). May indicate user rejection of unauthorized access.

Detects Silverfort AS-REP Roasting incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects AS-REQ messages without pre-authentication accepted by the domain controller. May indicate collection of AS-REP responses for offline password cracking.
Detects Silverfort SMB Enumeration incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects unusually high access to CIFS servers. May indicate reconnaissance of shared resources.

Detects Silverfort Bad Checksum in Kerberos incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects Kerberos authentication failures from checksum mismatches. May indicate tampering or forged packets.
Detects Silverfort Malicious IP incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects authentications from IPs flagged as malicious. May indicate attacker-controlled infrastructure.
Detects Silverfort Impossible Travel incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects logins from distant locations within a short time. May indicate credential compromise.
Detects Silverfort MFA Request Generation (MFA Bombing) incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects repeated denied MFA prompts. May indicate attacker coercing user approval.

Detects Silverfort Payload Injection incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects suspicious username patterns (e.g., long or special-character inputs). May indicate malicious input injection.

Detects Silverfort Suspected Kerberoasting incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects weakly encrypted service ticket requests. May indicate SPN ticket harvesting for brute-force attacks.

Detects Silverfort Remote Service Installation incidents. Silverfort describes this incident type as: Detects the creation of new system services on a host. May indicate remote code execution using tools like PSExec or PAExec.
Detects Silverfort Suspicious Addition to Privileged Group incidents.
Detects Silverfort Security Log Cleared on Domain Controller incidents.
Detects Silverfort Suspicious NTDS.dit Extraction incidents.
